messages:
IncidentsBot: PAGE: high-error-rate model warmup failures in us-west-2 — multiple OOMs + CUDA errors on runtime pool. Pager sent to oncall. https://redwood.inc/incident/2712345678 :rotating_light:
SRE Jamie: saw the page, looking now. Is this hitting hosted and dedicated?
Alex B: initial signal is warmup path for vm-model-x (v3.2.1) failing during deserialize/compile. Getting repeated: 'cudaErrorMemoryAllocation' and 'deserialization: invalid header'.
Maya R: I'm oncall, taking it. tagging @ML-Ops Ryan for model side context.
ML-Ops Ryan: that model had a quantize job rolled out last night, but shouldn't affect warmup. I'll pull the load artifacts.
SRE Jamie: error rates: 5xx spike to ~6% production-wide in us-west-2 for /v1/generate. Tail latency increased. Dedicated customers on the pool report 503s.
Support Lina: I've opened PSRs for two enterprise customers (ACME, NorthHealth) — they're getting model load errors in logs. Need incident comms.
Alex B: past few logs: ```
[2026-03-15T10:04:12Z] runtime warmup [pool-worker-12]: model vm-model-x:v3.2.1 deserialization failed: invalid magic header (0x0)
[2026-03-15T10:04:13Z] cudart: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T10:04:14Z] kernel compile timeout after 120s: nvrtc timed out
```
SRE Jamie: looks like three failure modes stacking: corrupted artifact (deser), insufficient GPU memory (OOM), and compile timeouts. Could be correlated with a kernel cache eviction job that ran at 10:00.
Maya R: mitigation plan proposals: 1) stop warmup on the affected pool; 2) scale down concurrency to reduce memory pressure; 3) failover traffic to us-east-1 for affected models; 4) try loading a fallback quantized variant. Any objections?
Alex B: agree. For immediate relief I'd prefer stop warmup + route new traffic to fallback model variant (vm-model-x-small). That avoids reloading heavy weights.
ML-Ops Ryan: vm-model-x-small exists (int8). Should be compatible for most requests. I'll stage it as a fallback.
SRE Jamie: executing now: `redwood runtime set-warmup --pool=us-west-2-runtime --enabled=false` -> returning 200. Stopping warmup.
SRE Jamie: `redwood route update --model=vm-model-x --fallback=vm-model-x-small --region=us-west-2` -> applied.
IncidentsBot: System note: automatic rollback disabled for vm-model-x in us-west-2 (change made by SRE Jamie).
Support Lina: Sending a customer-facing note: "We're seeing transient errors while loading some models in us-west-2; traffic is being routed to a fallback model; degraded performance may be observed. Engineers are actively mitigating." Will post to customers in 15m.
Maya R: observed immediate drop in 5xxs to ~1.2% after routing fallback. Tail latency improved but some requests still queue.
Alex B: I pulled a sample artifact from the failing node: checksum mismatch vs central store. Likely artifact corruption during the last deploy of the model binary. Upload job at 09:58 had a few retries.
ML-Ops Ryan: if artifact corrupt + kernel cache eviction + memory pressure — combination explains compile timeouts (missing cached kernels force nvrtc compile under memory pressure).
SRE Jamie: intermediate step: cordon the two nodes with highest OOMs and restart the runtime containers to purge fragmented GPU allocations: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain node/gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> planning restart.
Eng Oncall: FYI, we have a scheduled kernel cache eviction cron at 10:00 UTC — I've disabled future run for next 24h to avoid repeat.
Maya R: handoff note for next oncall at 10:30 PDT (30m): I'll stay until then, but @SRE Jamie will take lead after my handoff. Key actions outstanding: 1) confirm all corrupted artifacts replaced; 2) monitor for OOMs after restarts; 3) run a canary load against fallback & original model once artifacts fixed.
SRE Jamie: replacing artifacts now: pulled verified binaries, re-issued model deploys to pool. `redwood model deploy --model=vm-model-x --from-url=s3://models/verified/vm-model-x-v3.2.1.tar.gz` -> deploy started.
IncidentsBot: note: deploy triggered, estimated 4m rolling load.
Support Lina: customers updated. PSRs linked in the incident doc.
Maya R: quick checklist before handoff: health endpoints green for fallback, 5xx < 1.5%, no new OOMs in last 2m.
SRE Jamie: health checks passing, watch windows opening. I'll keep the fallback route until we've validated artifact integrity and warmup behavior.
Alex B: postmortem pointers: capture artifact upload logs, kernel-cache eviction timing, and per-node memory pressure. Also add a test for verifying artifact checksums post-upload.
ML-Ops Ryan: will add a preflight checksum verify to the model release pipeline.
SRE Jamie: summary for the timeline channel: "Mitigated model warmup failures in us-west-2 by stopping warmup, routing to int8 fallback, cordoning affected nodes, replacing corrupted artifacts, and restarting runtime containers. Customer impact limited to a spike of 5xx (~6%) for ~12 minutes; decreased to ~1% after fallback. Follow-ups: artifact checksum validation, adjust kernel-cache eviction schedule, and investigate memory fragmentation behaviors."
Maya R: handing off to SRE Jamie at 10:30 PDT. leaving notes in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
SRE Jamie: taking over. I'll kick off the follow-ups and draft a postmortem in the next 24h.
IncidentsBot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: SRE Jamie.
Support Lina: closing customer comms loop after final validation.
Alex B: adding logs and kube commands used to the incident doc snippet for later reference.
Maya R: thanks team.
SRE Jamie: thanks everyone. I'll update when warmup is re-enabled and all checks pass.
